notes: The prior latest release, including Level 2 framing, was saved on GitHub at archive/pre-unassigned-weights-v21 before changes. level3-approved-v20 remains the earlier accepted relative-effort baseline. Numbered ZIPs and versioned reports are preserved.

The first editor holds null allocation and shows three dashes. Confirm and Run are disabled. Waiting, guide and hint navigation do not fill or confirm weights. A deliberate move on any slider initializes a positive total of 100; the other two share the remainder within one rounding point. Native zero positions exist only for the unassigned UI, never as trial weights. Subsequent ranges reserve at least one percent.

The first question is How would you split the 100%? with a neutral collapsed operation hint and matching guide. Later low-effort help asks about the consequences of changing a share rather than prescribing more weight or balance. No preset, mandatory aim selector or automatic near-even reference is added.

Reset before first publication returns to blank; subsequent Reset restores the last actual allocation and clears confirmations. Two distinct observed tests still unlock comparison, with one optional cancellable third. Equal, never-equal and unchanged-effort histories can all finish. The game never claims an untested balanced solution was disproved.

The v20 effort model, proportional redistribution, criteria-stopping illustration, actual result dialogue, comparison, scene payloads and theory endpoint remain unchanged. Apart from the new initializer, weights.ts is byte-identical to the saved baseline. All 4851 positive splits, permutations, 28518 one-point transfers and slider edits are checked again; first initialization is also checked for every card and requested integer -2 through 102 plus invalid inputs.

Production browser paths exercise truly blank waiting, guide/hint neutrality, initial and later Reset, real ArrowRight/End/Home and pointer starts on every card, first-even and first-uneven observations, two uneven tests finishing without a near-even gate, unchanged effort, optional-third cancellation/reopening, extreme 98/1/1 and fresh reload. Layout/guide/comparison checks cover 1366/768/390/320 pixels, normal/reduced motion and hidden-page timing. Stable desktop and 320px unassigned screenshots were visually inspected after finite arrival animations.

Level 1, Level 2 and shared product source are unchanged from the saved baseline. Current Level 2 builds and actual ZIPs retain the six-metric question Would more metrics help Alex learn?, the 6-to-question-mark diagram, Test more metrics, continuous 10-to-25-to-100 growth and More metrics. Still chasing marks. Current Level 2 checks revalidate 3.5-second holds, anticipated turns, hidden-page pauses and normal/reduced-motion phone layouts.

Partner tests revalidate supplied names, original Level 2 trio and editable preselection, page-local sound, immutable copied observations, completion once, null comparisons for uniform-pattern histories and theory.reveal without Design Lab. The teammate’s authored animation scripts and scene request contracts are unchanged. The opening merge remains separate.

All four production builds and five latest ZIPs match the source/HTML/archive manifest hashes and byte comparisons. The review ZIP contains standalone Level 3 and connected Levels 1-to-2-to-3 from those builds. Release tests play actual packaged entries and the connected game offline.

Offline browser checks use exact production or packaged HTML served through an in-memory HTTPS route because managed Chromium blocks local file navigation. Direct opening in a particular user browser and classroom learning efficacy are not established. This report records 75 current functional/contract checks; older counts remain historical.
